chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs the ritual bath (ghusl) in Medina for the state of Ihram; does it suffice him - instead of the Ghusl of Dhi al-Hulayfah? He said, 'Yes.'
And these narrations came only as a concession (rukhsah) regarding the advancement of the bath - before the Miqat - for one who fears that he will not find water at the Miqat. He narrated that.

key_terms.الْمِيقَاتِ: The Miqat (ritual boundary/station for entering Ihram)
key_terms.تَقْدِيمِ الْغُسْلِ: Advancing / Performing the bath early (before reaching the Miqat)
key_terms.غُسْلِ ذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ: The Ghusl of Dhi al-Hulayfah (the specific ritual bath at the Miqat near Medina)
key_terms.لِلْإِحْرَامِ: For the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: Does it suffice him / Is it acceptable

ai.seo_question: Can I perform Ghusl for Ihram in Medina instead of at Dhi al-Hulayfah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that performing Ghusl al-Ihram in Medina is valid, serving as a specific concession (rukhsah) for travelers who fear water scarcity at the designated Miqat. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of facilitating ritual purity by allowing the bath to be taken slightly before the strict boundary if necessary, ensuring the pilgrim enters the state of Ihram without ritual impurity.
